You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Separator color is the color occupying complete rows/columns between tiles.
    sep_rows = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row)) == 1]
    sep_cols = [c for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] == grid[0][c] for r in range(h)) and len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1]
    # More generally, separators are the most frequent color when present as full lines.
    def runs(size, separators):
        groups = []
        start = 0
        for p in separators:
            if start < p:
                groups.append((start, p))
            start = p + 1
        if start < size:
            groups.append((start, size))
        return groups
    # Detect full separator lines by their shared color and repeated line pattern.
    # ARC separators here span the entire width/height and are single-color.
    if not sep_rows:
        colors = [v for row in grid for v in row]
        sep = max(set(colors), key=colors.count)
        sep_rows = [r for r,row in enumerate(grid) if all(v == sep for v in row)]
    if not sep_cols:
        colors = [v for row in grid for v in row]
        sep = max(set(colors), key=colors.count)
        sep_cols = [c for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] == sep for r in range(h))]
    row_groups, col_groups = runs(h, sep_rows), runs(w, sep_cols)
    values = [v for row in grid for v in row]
    sep_color = max(set(values), key=values.count)
    bg = max((v for v in set(values) if v != sep_color), key=lambda v: values.count(v))
    marker = next((v for v in set(values) if v not in (sep_color, bg)), None)
    out = []
    for r0, r1 in row_groups:
        outrow = []
        for c0, c1 in col_groups:
            count = sum(grid[r][c] == marker for r in range(r0, r1) for c in range(c0, c1))
            outrow.append(1 if count >= 2 else bg)
        out.append(outrow)
    return out

if __name__ == '__main__':
    demo = [[8,8,8,7,8,8,6,7,8,8,8,7,8,8,8],[6,8,8,7,8,8,8,7,6,8,8,7,6,8,8],[8,8,8,7,8,8,8,7,8,8,6,7,8,8,8],[7]*15,[8,8,8,7,8,8,8,7,8,8,6,7,8,8,8],[8,6,8,7,8,6,8,7,6,8,8,7,8,8,8],[8,8,8,7,8,8,8,7,8,8,8,7,6,8,8],[7]*15,[8,8,8,7,8,8,8,7,6,8,6,7,6,8,8],[8,6,8,7,6,8,8,7,8,8,8,7,8,8,8],[8,8,8,7,8,8,8,7,8,8,8,7,8,8,8],[7]*15,[8,8,8,7,6,8,8,7,6,8,8,7,8,6,8],[8,8,8,7,8,8,8,7,8,8,8,7,8,8,8],[8,6,8,7,8,6,8,7,8,8,8,7,8,6,8]]
    assert transform(demo) == [[8,8,1,8],[8,8,1,8],[8,8,1,8],[8,1,8,1]]
    test = [[2,2,4,9,2],[9,9,4,9,2],[4,4,4,4,4],[9,2,4,2,2],[2,2,4,2,9],[4,4,4,4,4],[2,9,4,2,2],[9,2,4,9,2]]
    print(transform(test))
    print('demo verified')
